author: WP10
summary: A short overview (rewritten for the d6e9ff05 synchronisation) contrasting the three non-GPU renderer contracts: SOFTWARE's real CPU pixels, HEADLESS's validation and trace without an image, and STUB's bare framework survival. Every claim is current at 009d40f5. libcna.com already covers all of it in more depth (Software, Headless and Stub internals pages, Tutorial 107 and the CPU renderers section), so the unit is absorbed as preserved knowledge with no new page.

concepts.text: SOFTWARE, PORTABLEGL, HEADLESS and STUB all run with no GPU, no driver and no display server, but they answer different questions: two produce real CPU pixels and two produce none at all.

PORTABLEGL's OpenGL-shaped CPU route is a separate family (a CPU implementation of an OpenGL 3.x-style pipeline) and is described with the GL renderers rather than with the hand-built SOFTWARE rasteriser.
tokens: PORTABLEGL: a real GL pipeline on the CPU

concepts.text: SOFTWARE owns colour, depth/stencil, multisample and texture storage in a CPU framebuffer, assembles and clips primitives, rasterises points, lines and triangles, applies depth, stencil, blend, sampling and stock-effect shading and offers deterministic back-buffer and target readback; there is no command queue, fence or device-loss model.
tokens: there is no command queue, fence or device-loss model

concepts.text: Presentation is not part of SOFTWARE's contract on windowing platforms: it stays off-screen and results are read back with GetBackBufferData(); only on CNA_PLATFORM=TERMINAL attached to a TTY does it hand frames to a surface presenter, so swap-chain and driver questions are non-applicable rather than failed.

SOFTWARE's evidence is broad public-fixture coverage (buffers, all primitive types, formats, textures, targets and MRT, MSAA, state, SpriteBatch and SpriteFont, stock effects, queries, lifetime), with many fixture sources shared with EasyGL, SDL_GPU and HEADLESS so results can be compared across renderers.

CPU raster coverage does not imply arbitrary user shaders: SOFTWARE reports CustomEffects false and never executes ShaderEffect source; compiled Effect Framework execution exists only in a build with CNA_SOFTWARE_COMPILED_EFFECTS.
tokens: CreateCompiledEffect returns null in a build without the option

concepts.text: HEADLESS validates arguments, resource ownership and lifetimes and keeps draw and state counters (optionally a structured trace), but never rasterises and makes no colour claim; ReadBackbuffer always throws NotSupportedException.

A HEADLESS pass proves that the game loop reaches draws with legal objects and in the expected order; it cannot prove geometry, shaders, sampling, blending or presentation, so a pixel question moves to SOFTWARE and a driver question to a real GPU renderer.
tokens: For a pixel mismatch move to Software for CPU pixels

concepts.text: HEADLESS resources keep enough state (shadow data, registry, statistics, debug labels) for deterministic lifecycle, leak and trace tests, which makes it useful for ContentManager, diagnostics and server-style runs, while a trace or counter remains weaker evidence than a rendered pixel.
tokens: HEADLESS: what your code did, not what it looked like

concepts.text: STUB is the minimal no-op family: every frame call, buffer upload, SpriteBatch call and colored draw is empty, so a successful run proves only that the caller respected the minimal construction contract.
STUB must not advertise capabilities merely because an inherited method returns: it answers false for every one of the 19 GraphicsCapability members, the honest end of the capability spectrum.
tokens: SupportsCapability returns false for every queried capability

concepts.text: Choose SOFTWARE for deterministic image assertions, HEADLESS for validation, counters and trace diffs, STUB for bare framework survival; a test should name which question it asks, because calling all three 'headless rendering' discards the evidence distinction (HEADLESS is also a platform value and a windowless mode of other renderers).

target.evidence: methodology; consistent with GraphicsAdapter::GetRequiredRendererEXT (UseNullDevice -> HEADLESS, UseReferenceDevice -> SOFTWARE)
